extracted.intended_audience: students of journalism and practicing reporters
extracted.subtask_description: Compare multiple newspaper accounts of the same event (here, pageant/parade reports) to identify differences in style, tone, voice, and selection of detail. Use paired examples (e.g., New York Herald vs. New York World) to analyze how different approaches shape reader impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: style and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Note — The next two stones, which describe a pageant parade, should be compared with reference to style and tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the paired accounts (New York Herald and New York World) for differences in narrative voice and tone (e.g., straightforward factual reporting vs. colorful/ironic commentary), selection and ordering of facts, use of descriptive imagery and figurative language, inclusion of human-interest details, and the overall effect on the reader. Use the two pieces as exemplars to discuss how style and tone alter emphasis and audience perception.
